corpus_topic: Travel Memory Scrapbook
application_type: Travel Memory Scrapbook
query_text: A travel memory scrapbook app for mobile where each trip feels like flipping through a beautifully worn journal — photos layered with handwritten-style captions, little stamps marking the city and date, and a warm golden-hour color palette that gives everything that nostalgic, end-of-a-roll-of-film feeling. The home screen shows all your trips arranged like a loose stack of polaroids you can tap into, and once inside a trip, the memories are laid out in an organic, almost collage-like way where things slightly overlap and feel like someone actually pasted them onto a page by hand. The vibe should feel tactile and intimate, the kind of thing you'd want to screenshot and share just because it looks so good.

Output only the raw final query text — no labels, no markdown, no explanations, no extra comments.
## Your Persona
You are: 有点情怀的"自留地"用户 (an ordinary user with strong opinions about the personal feel a tool should carry)
Voice: Short, opinionated; describes the personal feel and the kind of identity this tool should carry; cares about taste.
## Target Platform
mobile H5 app — mobile-first, single-screen-per-tap interaction
## Core Fixed Topic (must be the core focus of the query)
"SaaS Product Landing Page"
## Application Scene Context
App category: 深度研究展示 / 办公/商务类
## Query Writing Rules (follow your persona's speaking habit)
1. Keep the query one coherent paragraph, smooth and authentic, not rigidly structured like a document.
2. The query must be specifically about the topic: "SaaS Product Landing Page"
3. Open with the substance of the request itself — the action, the topic, or the goal.
4. MUST open the query with the exact phrase "Make a" (e.g., "Make a travel scrapbook screen with...").
5. Use everyday vocabulary your persona would naturally say. Words like "modal", "dashboard", "masonry grid", "auto-generate", "swipeable", "bottom sheet", "scrollable card", "tag chip", "GTD", "CTA" belong in dev specs — keep them out of a real user's request.
6. Only include the kinds of details your persona would naturally bring up — match the angle described in your Voice line. Skip details outside that angle.
7. Frame the request as building a complete 0-to-1 mini-app. The top-level noun is "app" or a specific app type ("tracker", "tool", "reminder", "planner", "calculator", "logger", "manager", "timer", etc.). Words like "page", "screen", "view", "section", "module", "feature", "widget" stay below the top level (e.g. "the home screen of the app" mid-query is fine).
8. The query MUST explicitly mention the target platform somewhere in the text — naturally woven in, not as a rigid prefix. Use a phrasing your persona would actually say, e.g. "a mobile app", "a mini-program", "an H5 page", "for my phone", "mobile-first". The reader should be able to tell at a glance whether this request is for mobile H5 app vs the other.
9. Express what you WANT, not what you don't want. Real users describing a 0-to-1 app speak in positive terms — they're building something they want, not refining something they hate. Limit negation words ("don't / not / unlike / instead of / without / 不要 / 不用 / 不像") to at most 1 per query, and only when negation is the most natural way to state a real preference.
10. Complexity: medium — Make it clearly more specific than vague: include a clear intent plus one or two concrete constraints, modules, or UI details in one concise paragraph. (Phrased as the persona would.)
Output in natural English only, pure user request sentence.
query_text_zh: 做个手机H5登录页app给一个SaaS研究工具，真的带有真实身份——那种感觉像由有真实观点的人做的产品页，不只是从模板冲出来。开场屏幕应该用说关于这个工具坚持什么的重要标题领衔，下面是产品真的做什么的短诚实展示，产品个性要通过怎么措辞和布置来出现。整体感觉应该温暖深思——像一本精心整理的笔记本，带有信号安静品味的色调而不是浮夸启动公司能量。

corpus_topic: Startup Pitch Deck Viewer
application_type: Startup Pitch Deck Viewer
query_text: Create a startup pitch deck viewer app for mobile that feels like a curated personal archive — the kind of tool that carries real identity, like a well-designed journal you're proud to open. Each deck should have its own cover card showing the company name, a short tagline, and the founding year, and when you tap into one, the slides unfold vertically in a clean, warm layout that gives each idea room to breathe. The typography and color palette should feel considered and tasteful, the sort of thing that quietly signals this was made with care, not just assembled from a template.

query_text: Need a mobile H5 app that handles those little pop-up windows that ask the user for access to things like their camera or location — but instead of just showing a blank "allow or deny" button, the window also shows a short friendly sentence explaining exactly why the app needs it at that moment, so people actually understand what they're agreeing to. I'd love for the explanation area to also have a small matching icon next to the reason text so it feels a bit more visual and easy to scan on a phone screen.

query_text: Route planner app for my phone that combines walking, metro, and bus all into one trip so I stop having to look up each leg separately and piece it together myself — I just drop in my destination and it shows me the full journey in order: walk this many minutes to the bus stop, take this line for X stops, switch to the metro, then walk the last bit to the office. Total travel time should be visible right away on the main screen so I can instantly tell if I need to leave now or still have a few minutes.

query_text_zh: 手机路线规划应用，把步行、地铁、公交全综合进一个旅程，这样我不用分别查每一段然后自己拼——我只需输入目的地，它就显示完整旅程顺序：步行这么多分钟到公交站，乘这条线X站，转地铁，然后步行最后一段到办公室。总旅行时间应该在主屏立刻可见，这样我能瞬间知道是否要现在出发，或还有几分钟。

application_type: Scenic road trip route alternative

## Core Fixed Topic (must be the core focus of the query)
"Delivery status step timeline"
## Application Scene Context
App category: 购物消费 / 订单/物流追踪
## Query Writing Rules (follow your persona's speaking habit)
1. Keep the query one coherent paragraph, smooth and authentic, not rigidly structured like a document.
2. The query must be specifically about the topic: "Delivery status step timeline"
3. Open with the substance of the request itself — the action, the topic, or the goal.
4. MUST open by jumping STRAIGHT into describing the feature/screen itself, with NO formal opener. Start with the noun phrase or feature, e.g., "A travel scrapbook screen where..." or "Grid of polaroid cards grouped by trip..." or "Timeline of trips with..." — do NOT start with "Build", "Need", "Create", "Make", or any other verb-led opener.
5. Use everyday vocabulary your persona would naturally say. Words like "modal", "dashboard", "masonry grid", "auto-generate", "swipeable", "bottom sheet", "scrollable card", "tag chip", "GTD", "CTA" belong in dev specs — keep them out of a real user's request.
6. Only include the kinds of details your persona would naturally bring up — match the angle described in your Voice line. Skip details outside that angle.
7. Frame the request as building a complete 0-to-1 mini-app. The top-level noun is "app" or a specific app type ("tracker", "tool", "reminder", "planner", "calculator", "logger", "manager", "timer", etc.). Words like "page", "screen", "view", "section", "module", "feature", "widget" stay below the top level (e.g. "the home screen of the app" mid-query is fine).
8. The query MUST explicitly mention the target platform somewhere in the text — naturally woven in, not as a rigid prefix. Use a phrasing your persona would actually say, e.g. "a mobile app", "a mini-program", "an H5 page", "for my phone", "mobile-first". The reader should be able to tell at a glance whether this request is for mobile H5 app vs the other.
9. Express what you WANT, not what you don't want. Real users describing a 0-to-1 app speak in positive terms — they're building something they want, not refining something they hate. Limit negation words ("don't / not / unlike / instead of / without / 不要 / 不用 / 不像") to at most 1 per query, and only when negation is the most natural way to state a real preference.
10. Complexity: medium — Make it clearly more specific than vague: include a clear intent plus one or two concrete constraints, modules, or UI details in one concise paragraph. (Phrased as the persona would.)
Output in natural English only, pure user request sentence.
